title: Sampling and Extraction of Lyophilized Plant Tissue for LC-MS Analysis
author: Kateřina Kučerová
materials: Preparation of Sampling Materials and Equipment 50 mL Falcon tubes, a scalpel or knife, scissors, 96 % ethanol for surface sterilization, disposable gloves for handling, a transport box containing dry ice.
Preparation of Materials and Equipment for Extraction EtOH-H 2 O (75:25) CH 3 CN-H 2 O (50:50) 2.0 mL Eppendorf tubes Stainless steel grinding beads Pipettes with tips (100–1000 μL] Labels.

steps.title: Sample Collection and Transport
steps.instruction: Collect fresh plant tissue and transport it to the laboratory while maintaining sample integrity.

substeps.instruction: Cut a defined portion of fresh plant tissue (e.g., leaf, root, stem, flower, or fruit).
Immediately transfer the tissue into a sterile 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Immediately place the tubes on dry ice.

steps.title: Lyophilization Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the centrifuge tubes for the lyophilization process.

substeps.instruction: Cover the tube opening with a single piece of fine mesh fabric to allow airflow and prevent contamination.
Secure the mesh fabric with a rubber band.

steps.title: Lyophilization
steps.instruction: Dry the plant tissue using a lyophilizer.

substeps.instruction: Place the prepared tubes into the lyophilizer flasks in a stable, upright position.
Perform lyophilization for 3 days, following the manufacturer’s operating guidelines.

steps.title: Tissue Grinding and Storage
steps.instruction: Convert the lyophilized material into a homogeneous powder and store it.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the lyophilized plant material into an analytical mill and grind to a fine, homogeneous powder.
Store the ground material in a tightly sealed Falcon tube under dry room conditions.

steps.title: Initial Sample Homogenization
steps.instruction: Prepare and homogenize a specific mass of lyophilized material.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 25 ± 2.5 mg of lyophilized plant material into a 2.0 mL round-bottom Eppendorf tube.
Add one stainless steel grinding bead to each tube.
Homogenize the samples using a TissueLyser at 25 rpm for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Solvent Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract compounds from the homogenized tissue using an ethanol-water solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 000 μL of EtOH-H2O solution (75:25, v/v) to each tube and vortex briefly.
Incubate the samples at 40 °C for 3 minutes.
Homogenize the samples using a TissueLyser at 25 rpm for 60 seconds.

steps.title: Primary Clarification and Concentration
steps.instruction: Separate the extract from debris and remove the solvent.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the samples at 14 000 rpm for 5 minutes to pellet debris.
Carefully transfer 500 μL of the supernatant into a new 2.0 mL Eppendorf tube, avoiding particulate matter.
Evaporate the solvent using a SpeedVac concentrator until completely dry.

steps.title: Resuspension and Final Clarification
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried extract and clarify it for LC-MS analysis.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the dried extract in 2 000 μL of CH3CN-H2O solution (50:50, v/v).
Sonicate the samples for 15 seconds, then vortex for 30 seconds.
Centrifuge the samples at 14 000 rpm for 5 minutes to clarify the extract.
Carefully transfer the clarified supernatant into LC-MS vials, avoiding residual particulates.
